_about: Where the scout rover can be sent, what it reports, and the special ores (scout update). Positions are Godot metres (x east, z south). Site reports are game story written for ages 9-12; mineral facts cite the entries in data/model_sources_scout.json. A survey reveals every ore deposit within reveal_radius_m of the site on the map; deposits can also be found by walking.

sites.name: East plain
sites.report: Flat, firm ground covered in small dark pebbles, next to an old rover that broke down here. The mast camera sees round grey beads in the soil: they look like hematite, an iron mineral. Good walking ground.
sites.rover_note: A crew rover could drive here easily.

sites.name: Old crash site
sites.report: Twisted metal from an old landing that went wrong. Sharp edges everywhere. Near the walls of the base the ground has greenish rock: it looks like olivine.
sites.hazard: Sharp metal: walk carefully, keep the suit safe.
sites.rover_note: Drive around the debris, not through it.

sites.name: South slope
sites.terrain: A gentle slope of light-coloured rock.
sites.report: Bright white lines run through the rock like cracks filled with chalk. They look like gypsum, a mineral that forms where water once flowed.
sites.rover_note: A crew rover can climb it slowly.

sites.name: West dunes
sites.report: Rippled sand dunes, soft and deep. At the edge of the sand there is pale, crumbly rock that fizzes in the lab test: it looks like carbonate.
sites.hazard: Soft sand: wheels can sink and get stuck.
sites.rover_note: Keep a crew rover out of the deep sand.

sites.name: Little crater
sites.terrain: A small crater with a steep rim.
sites.report: A small crater about 30 metres across. Its rim shows layers of rock, like the pages of a book: each layer is a different time in Mars history. Too far to walk to safely in a suit.
sites.hazard: Steep rim: too far to walk.
sites.rover_note: A good first trip for the crew rover, once it is built.

hematite.name: Hematite
hematite.what: An iron mineral. On Mars it can form small round beads.
hematite.why: Iron for simple metal parts: two hematite make one spare part at the workbench.

olivine.name: Olivine
olivine.what: A green mineral found in volcanic rock.
olivine.why: Science: it tells us how the rock formed. Each one studied raises the colony's science score.

gypsum.name: Gypsum
gypsum.what: A soft white mineral that forms when salty water dries up.
gypsum.why: Science: proof that water once flowed here. Each one studied raises the colony's science score.

carbonate.name: Carbonate rock
carbonate.what: Rock that forms in water, like chalk and limestone on Earth.
carbonate.why: Science: places like this are where scientists look for signs of ancient life. Each one studied raises the colony's science score.
